items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 only says 'square plate'; Sec. 4.1 states 'The length is fixed at L = 1.0 m' for all three problems, but which plate dimension L denotes (side = L or a multiple of L) is shown only in Fig. 6a. Because ℓ = 0.008 and h_min/h_max are absolute lengths, the side length changes the relative regularization length and resolution.
readings: side = L = 1.0 m (1.0 m x 1.0 m)

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1: 'square plate being fixed at Γ_u as shown in Fig. (6a)'. The text never says where Γ_u lies on the square.
readings: two separate supports at the two bottom corners

items.entity: fixed boundary Γ_u – length/extent along the edge
items.description: The text doesn't say whether Γ_u is a whole edge, a partial segment or point-like supports, or give its length/position along the edge (Fig. 6a only). The support type itself (u = 0) is given.
readings: half of the edge (0.5L) adjacent to one corner

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 calls the plate 'asymmetrically loaded' but gives no location for Γ_t (which edge, offset as a fraction of L, number of loaded segments). Eq. (39) only names Γ_t; the position is in Fig. 6a.
readings: right edge at the bottom corner (y = 0)
right edge at the top corner (y = L)

items.entity: traction on Γ_t – loaded length and distribution
items.description: The load is a boundary traction t on Γ_t (Eq. 39, |t| given in N/m), but the length of Γ_t is not stated. On a structured grid it could be a nodal point load or a uniform traction over a short segment.
readings: concentrated load at a single node

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the magnitude |t| = 1.0e3 N/m; the direction of t appears only in Fig. 6a.

|t| = 1.0e3 N/m (Sec. 4.1) is a line-traction density. The resultant force depends on the figure-only length of Γ_t and the implied unit out-of-plane depth (plane strain, no thickness given), so the nodal force to apply is not fixed.
readings: uniform traction 1.0e3 N/m along Γ_t, resultant = 1.0e3·|Γ_t| N per metre depth
resultant force 1.0e3 N (per metre depth) applied as a nodal/point load

items.entity: solid condition at loaded boundary Γ_t
items.description: Sec. 2.2/Sec. 3 and the A.1 evolution problem impose φ = 1 on G_t (load boundary kept solid). But the A.1 weak form of the standard wave equation used in Sec. 4.1.1 states φ_{v+1} = 0 on G_t. The nodal Dirichlet condition also has no stated passive-element width for a structured grid. No other non-design regions are mentioned for Fig. 6a.
readings: φ = 1 on Γ_t -> one row of passive solid elements along the loaded segment
φ = 1 only at the loaded boundary nodes -> no passive elements in a density solver
φ = 0 on Γ_t (A.1 weak form) -> loaded edge lies on the interface, not forced solid

items.entity: 2D stress state (plane strain vs plane stress)
items.description: Plane strain is stated only in the general formulation (Sec. 2.1, Lamé constants 'in plane strain assumption'). Sec. 4.1 doesn't restate it, while Sec. 4.3 explicitly switches to plane stress for its example. Plane strain with ν = 0.3 equals plane stress with ν* ≈ 0.43 and E* = E/(1-ν^2), which is not a pure scaling.

Sec. 4.1 gives only an adaptive element-size range, h_min = 5e-4 to h_max = 1.0e-2 (units not stated, presumably m), on an unstructured FreeFEM++/mmg mesh. No uniform grid size, element type/order or remeshing criterion is given for a structured-grid re-run.

No density or sensitivity filter is given. Regularization comes only from the ℓ^2∇^2φ term of the wave-equation update (ℓ = 0.008, a length; Sec. 3 and 4.1.1). The equivalent filter radius or projection for a density-based structured solver is not given.
readings: PDE/Helmholtz filter with length ℓ = 0.008 m (r_min ≈ 2√3·ℓ ≈ 0.028 m)
density filter radius r_min = ℓ = 0.008 m
conventional r_min of about 1.5-3 element widths
no filter; implement the paper's standard wave-equation level-set update (ℓ = 0.008, m = 0, k = 0, Δv = 1)

items.entity: Heaviside transition parameter β – values run
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says β 'is varied between β = 2.0 and β = 8.0'; the actual β values appear only in Fig. 7. β scales the driving term and the Heaviside width. Sec. 4.1.5 shows β can change complexity/symmetry, although Sec. 4.1.1 reports nearly identical layouts here.
Sec. 4.1: r 'is increased in each iteration until it reaches a limit value r_max'. Initial λ, initial r, the increase rule and r_max are not given.

items.entity: multiplier update and multiplier used in perturbation term f_1
items.description: Sec. 4.1 updates λ = λ' + r·max{G; 0} (never decreases). This is inconsistent with the AL form Ḡ = max{G; -λ'/r} defined in the same section and with Sec. 4.3's λ = max{λ' + r g; 0}. It is also unclear whether f_1 = (λ + rG) I_G / V_0 - ... uses the updated λ or the previous λ'.
readings: λ <- λ' + r·max{G, 0}; f_1 uses the updated λ
λ <- max{λ' + rG, 0} (standard AL); f_1 uses the previous λ'
λ <- max{λ' + rG, 0}; f_1 uses the updated λ

items.description: Eq. (44) integrates an L2(D) norm over D, C_v = (1/(c_f V_0)) ∫_D |∂R/∂Θ|_{L2(D)} dΩ. It can be read as the L2 norm divided by c_f or as the mean absolute value. Either way it sets the step size of S_v = f_v β / C_v (c_f = 1.0 given).
Sec. 4.1 uses 'a completely filled design domain' for φ_0 and φ_{-1} but gives no φ value. φ is defined in [-1, 1] (Sec. 2.1), yet the update (Eq. 32 / A.1) states no clipping or truncation step.
readings: φ_0 = φ_{-1} = 1, φ clipped to [-1, 1] after each update
φ_0 = φ_{-1} = small positive constant (e.g. 0.1), clipped to [-1, 1]

items.description: Sec. 3 / Fig. 5: the loop ends at 'convergence to a minimum' or 'a predefined number of iterations', but neither a tolerance nor an iteration limit is given. The iteration range of the convergence histories appears only in Fig. 7.
readings: stop when relative change of J < 1e-4 and |G| < 1e-3 over several iterations
